text:
Sam: heads up — customer "AtlasHealth" (private VPC) asked if we can rebill them for cloud egress + 3rd-party marketplace license for GPU drivers. They want raw pass-through line items on the invoice. Is that allowed?

Maria: @Sam quick q: is this customer on Dedicated or Private? For Private we usually invoice for Redwood-managed infra + pass-through (cloud network egress) as separate lines, but marketplace AMI license we've been bundling. Need to check.

Sam: Private (VPC), they've got their own cloud account but want us to show charges as if we invoiced them directly — they want to pass our reserved capacity cost to internal business unit.

Priya: From sales POV they want transparency for their auditors. We can add line items for 'third-party pass-through' but legal/finance need to confirm licensing T&Cs. Some marketplace licenses forbid reselling.

Tom: Infra note: if they're using our images that include vendor-provided drivers (NVIDIA GRID/Enterprise) the license fee is billed on the marketplace subscription to our account. There's a flag to enable 'customer-billed' if we switch to BYOL (bring-your-own-license) AMI, but that changes onboarding complexity.

Legal: We can't re-bill a vendor charge unless the vendor EULA permits transfer. Need to see exact license (NVIDIA/Red Hat). Can we require the customer to accept a marketplace subscription in their cloud console? That would let them pay vendor directly.

Maria: Action items: 1) Finance to confirm whether our billing system can expose raw provider line items per-customer for private/VPC. 2) Legal to review vendor T&Cs for re-billing. 3) Sales to offer BYOL or vendor-direct path as an option.

BillingBot: FYI — current invoice schema supports custom lines labeled 'pass-through' and we can add metadata like provider and original invoice id.

Priya: Is there a price floor for reserved capacity we need to communicate? Some customers assume reserved commit is fully transferable to them.

Sam: Good point — committed Reserved Capacity is contractual between Redwood and cloud provider. We can allocate cost attribution to customers but can't transfer the contractual liability unless we set up dedicated committed contracts on their billing account.

Tom: Region constraint: for APAC clusters some providers tie marketplace licensing to account region, complicating direct pass-through. That came up with HK region last month.

Legal: I'll review both NVIDIA and Marketplace terms. If we can't rebill, we should prepare a standard clause and an FAQ explaining options (BYOL, vendor-direct, or bundling).

Maria: I'll confirm with Finance by EOD whether adding visible pass-through lines is OK for compliance. @BillingBot can you pull a sample invoice with pass-through line for AtlasHealth test account?

BillingBot: Requested sample generated: https://invoices.redwood.internal/sample/atlas-pass-through-1765123456 (internal link)

Sam: Thanks — will forward to the customer. If legal OKs, we might add an option in onboarding to toggle 'customer pays vendor directly' vs 'Redwood itemizes and collects'.

Priya: Marking as blocking for onboarding. :white_check_mark:

Tom: Also note: if they want license support L2 from vendor we need to coordinate support contact flow.

Legal: Will follow up in a separate thread with clause language.

Sam: closing loop here once we get legal + finance. Thanks everyone :handshake:
